newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end up at record high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end up at record high.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended up 1.08 percent on Monday at a record 724.56 points on the back of continuing strong fundamentals in the economy, brokers and analysts said.
The index rose 7.73 points during the day, with advancers leeading decliners by 80 to 49, with 62 issues unchanged. Total turn-over was estimated at 721 billion rupiah.
"The opportunities for further upside are there. The index could even go over 750 points later this year," Laksono Widodo, an analyst with brokerage firm PT ING Baring Securities Indonesia, said.
The World Bank's chief representative in Indonesia last Monday predicted the country's growth would continue to be strong over the next year, although little had been done to reduce domestic risk.
Dennis de Tray told reporters he expected economic growth to be about 7.75 percent this year and he saw "an overall healthy picture for the next six to 12 months".
Brokers said Mondays's strong showing also reflected the increasing weight of local players who now account for around 55 percent of daily trading volume.
"Despite the public holiday in Hong Kong, the market remained active with high trading volume. I think the local mutual fund managers were largely involved in the market today," one broker said.
Brokers said the sharp rise was partly due to active blue-chip buying in cement firms, including Indocement and Semen Gresik, and cigarette firms Gudang Garam and Sampoerna.

Bakrieland topped the active list with 69 million shares traded as it fell 175 rupiah to 1,950 rupiah on profit-taking. It had risen sharply last week on market talk that it would be involved in the construction of a mass rapid transportation project, brokers said.
